title: Facebook Ad Agency Pricing: Fees and Budget
summary: Compare Facebook ad agency pricing with published management fees, creative costs and a copyable quote worksheet. Build a budget that includes media spend.
body_markdown:
## When is an agency fee worth paying?


Evaluate the fee against the work it removes and the business result you need to assess. Name the current gap: campaign ownership, creative capacity, measurement or several of these. Then ask for a first-month plan that connects the purchased work to that gap. Use our[agency selection guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) to review the supporting evidence.


If your media buyer is ready to launch tests but keeps waiting for ads, compare a dedicated production scope before replacing the whole team. If campaigns have no accountable owner, a production-only quote leaves that job open. A cheaper invoice can leave more work with your team; a larger invoice should explain exactly what additional responsibility it buys.


## How do you compare quotes across three realistic months?


Calculate a starting month, an ordinary month and a changed-scope month. A single monthly total can hide setup charges, spend thresholds or extra production. Ask the agency to confirm which assumptions change the bill before treating a forecast as a quote.


The following is an invented comparison to demonstrate the method. It is not a Knowlify price or a description of any named provider. Suppose Agency A charges a $1,800 management retainer and $1,200 for the agreed creative scope, with $600 setup. Agency B charges the greater of $1,000 or 12% of media spend, plus $1,500 creative and $900 setup. Assume the creative scope is genuinely equivalent for this example.


Scenario Agency A service cost Agency B service cost


First month at $10,000 media spend $1,800 + $1,200 + $600 = $3,600 $1,200 + $1,500 + $900 = $3,600


Ongoing month at $10,000 media spend $3,000 $2,700


Ongoing month at $20,000 media spend $3,000 $2,400 + $1,500 = $3,900


Media spend is additional in every row. The comparison changes as spend changes, even though both fictional quotes have the same first-month service total. Neither is inherently better: the actual decision still depends on equivalent responsibilities, delivery and the budget you expect to use.


Add a fourth scenario if you expect the creative workload to change. Ask what happens when you need a new product concept rather than another version of an existing ad. A predictable management fee does not make an undefined production scope predictable.


## Which exclusions can make the headline quote incomplete?


Look for work your campaign requires but the proposal leaves unassigned. Examples to investigate include product capture, creator logistics, additional edits, new language versions, landing-page changes and measurement implementation. This is a review list, not a claim that every agency charges separately for every item.


Put each required task into one of three categories: included in the service fee, separately quoted or retained by your team. An item described as “available” belongs in the separately quoted category until the proposal confirms inclusion. An item your team can handle still needs a realistic owner and workload estimate.


Compare rights and acceptance terms in the same way. If one production quote includes an agreed advertising-use period and another leaves usage unresolved, the lower total is not yet a complete comparison. Request the actual agreement and have the relevant reviewer resolve the difference. Do not insert an assumed rights price into a supposedly verified total.


Finally, distinguish optional work from necessary work. A supplier may offer a broad set of services that your campaign does not need. Adding every available option can make an otherwise focused scope hard to evaluate. Start with the work required for the planned campaign and document the conditions under which an additional service would become useful.


## How should you value work retained by your team?


Keep an internal-work estimate beside the cash budget. Use your company's own planning rate and actual expected hours rather than a generic agency benchmark. The goal is to expose workload, not to manufacture an exact economic return from uncertain inputs.


As an illustrative calculation, assume your team expects eight hours of briefing and review at a planning rate of $70 per hour. That is $560 of internal time in the comparison. If another arrangement requires twelve hours, its corresponding estimate is $840. Those invented figures do not establish that the first arrangement is better; they identify a $280 planning difference to investigate alongside the service scope.


Revisit the estimate after the first assignment. Record the hours spent supplying assets, consolidating feedback and resolving handoffs. If a low service fee consistently leaves substantial unplanned work with your team, use that evidence when requesting a revised scope. If your internal process creates the delay, address that instead of assuming a larger agency fee will solve it.


## What should the final price decision record?


Write down the selected scope, expected monthly cash budget, separate media budget and assumptions that could change the total. Record setup costs once and identify recurring charges explicitly. Ask the supplier to confirm unresolved items before the agreement is signed.


For Knowlify, request a private proposal for end-to-end Meta creative and campaign management, or creative-only support if you retain your buyer. Apply the same worksheet and scenario method to that proposal. Keep a copy of the agreed output definitions so later conversations about volume, revisions or campaign responsibility use the same terms.


Review actual invoices against the agreed scope after the first billing period. Resolve discrepancies as specific line items. A clear fee decision is one you can explain from the work purchased and the assumptions used, rather than from a headline monthly number alone.


For a Knowlify proposal, bring your completed worksheet, current creative volume and the roles your team already covers.[Discuss your Meta ads scope](https://knowlify.com/book) for creative and[campaign management](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency) together, or request creative-only support. Record finished ads, revisions, campaign responsibilities and separate media spend so you can compare the private quote with other proposals.


## FAQ


### What is the average Facebook ad agency fee?


The published examples in this guide are not a representative survey, so averaging them would be misleading. Use the stated fee formula at your own media budget, then compare included work. A management retainer, a creator-video package and a full-service engagement buy different responsibilities even when their monthly prices look similar.


### Is Facebook ad spend included in the agency fee?


Treat media spend as a separate budget unless the proposal explicitly bundles it. Ask for the amount allocated to ad delivery and the amount retained for services. That separation lets you distinguish a change in campaign spending from a change in the agency's fee and avoids counting the same cost twice.


### Does a percentage-of-spend fee include creative?


The percentage alone does not tell you. Require the proposal to name included concepts, scripts, finished ads, revisions and export formats. Also record what triggers an extra charge. If the agency only manages campaigns, add a separate production quote or the cost of creating assets in-house.


### Is a flat fee better than a percentage of spend?


Choose based on the written scope and your planned budget changes. A fixed fee makes the service bill predictable within its limits; a percentage model requires recalculating the bill as spend grows. Compare both at your current budget and your next planned level, including minimums, tiers and creative charges.


### What should I check before signing an agency contract?


Check delivery definitions, access, usage rights, revision limits, minimum term, cancellation and handover. Name who owns tracking, approves claims and authorizes budget changes. If there is a performance guarantee, record its measurement period, eligibility conditions and remedy in the agreement before relying on it.


### How much does Knowlify cost?

Prepare your formats, desired output, approval process and existing team responsibilities. Media spend is separate. Use the worksheet above to compare the agreed scope with other providers' proposals.
